newsitem.title: USA: Sprint buoyed by WTO deal, others follow.
newsitem.headline: Sprint buoyed by WTO deal, others follow.

text.p: Shares in Sprint Corp jumped more than four percent on Tuesday, leading a broad rise in U.S. long distance stocks after the World Trade Organisation (WTO) deal to open up telecommunication markets was signed at the weekend, analysts said.
Sprint was 1-7/8 higher at 44-1/2 at 1545 EDT/2045 GMT, in moderate volume. AT&T Corp was 5/8 firmer at 40-1/4 and MCI Communications Corp up 1/4 at $36.
"This deal is a long term positive, but it won't double anybody's profits overnight," said analyst Tony Ferrugia at brokers A.G. Edwards.
Sprint was also boosted by final approval by the EU early in the day of Global One, its ambitious alliance with Deutsche Telekom AG and France Telecom.

The WTO agreement reached over the weekend allows the $600 billion global telecom market to be gradually opened to competition, a plus for those U.S. long distance companies which already have international alliances.
"Many of the major markets are moving in this direction anyway," said Ferrugia.
MCI is in the process of merging with British Telecommunications Plc, while AT&T has a loose alliance called Unisource with four European national telecom companies.
